title: Add compliance-proof-bundler: signed audit receipts and KMS binding generator
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Add a new compliance-proof-bundler component that emits signed audit receipts per-tenant and a KMS binding generator to produce verifiable key provenance artifacts. Backwards compatible and disabled behind feature flag. Admins can opt into proof export in Redwood Console.
description: Context: Customers and compliance teams requested cryptographically verifiable audit receipts that prove which KMS key and RBAC decision were used for sensitive inference requests. Motivation: reduce time-to-evidence for audits and make region- and key-scoping claims auditable without shipping raw payloads. What this PR adds: a small long-running service (compliance-proof-bundler) that subscribes to the audit stream, groups events into tenant-scoped bundles, attaches KMS provenance assertions (key id, provider, region) generated by the KMS binding generator, signs a compact receipt using a durable site signing key, and emits an opaque, timestamped proof artifact to the audit store and optionally to S3/tenant export endpoints. It also adds an RBAC v2 policy annotator shim that records the exact policy fingerprint and decision path used for each decision included in a bundle, and a lightweight policy explainability stub returned in proofs for compliance review. Feature flag and admin controls: component is disabled by default. Console exposes a per-tenant toggle, export retention policy, and a dry-run mode for operators to evaluate proofs without publishing. KMS integrations: pluggable adapters added for AWS KMS and an HSM provider; adapters validate key metadata, canonicalize region claims, and produce a signed key-reference blob consumed by the bundler. Data residency: bundles include a region assertion derived from request routing plus KMS key region; we surface mismatches as warnings in the proof metadata. Security model: bundler runs as a dedicated service with least-privilege credentials, only reads audit stream and KMS metadata, and signs using a site-level hardware-protected signing key; RBAC annotator enforces that only authorized operator roles can request proof exports. Implementation notes: added services/audit/proof_bundler.go, pkg/compliance/kms_adapter.go, pkg/rbac/annotator.go, deploy/helm/templates/proof-bundler.yaml, docs/compliance/proof-bundler.md, integrations/private-installer/proof-export-hook.patch, e2e tests under test/e2e/proofs. Backwards compatibility: bundler does not modify existing audit messages; it subscribes and produces separate proof artifacts and therefore is non-invasive. Testing: unit tests for adapters and annotator, integration test exercising AWS KMS adapter in local emulator, e2e that verifies a signed receipt can be validated with the site public key. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag 1) internal staging, 2) canary tenants with dry-run=true, 3) opt-in enterprise tenants, 4) global opt-in. Monitoring and alerts: added metrics for bundle latency, proof-signing failures, adapter validation errors, and a console dashboard template. Risks and mitigations: signing key compromise mitigated by HSM rotation policy and key-use auditing; proof exposure mitigated by tenant-level access controls and optional export encryption. Related work: follows ENG-4821 and policy work in PM-993. Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests, [x] e2e tests (canary), [x] docs, [x] console toggle, [x] helm chart, [x] security review requested.

review_comments: Daniel Kim: Please add a clear migration/rollback path for disabling the feature in case we need to stop proof emission urgently.
Asha Patel: Added rollback docs and a hard-disable env var; updated rollout plan to include emergency-stop procedure.
Priya Rao: What prevents leakage of request payloads in receipts? We should ensure proofs never contain raw user data.

Asha Patel: Proof artifacts contain only references (request IDs, timestamps), KMS key metadata, RBAC fingerprints and signed hashes of canonicalized request metadata; explicitly do not include raw prompts or outputs. Added unit tests asserting no payload strings are serialized.
Samir Gupta: CI flaked on the HSM adapter test in the first run; make the test tolerant of local HSM timing.
Asha Patel: Adjusted integration test timeouts and added a retry helper around HSM startup in CI config.
ci_log: CI run 1: lint OK, unit tests OK, integration (HSM) failed (timeout); rerun triggered. CI run 2: all checks passed including e2e. Coverage delta +2.1% for compliance package.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature with `COMPLIANCE_PROOFS_ENABLED=true` and configure PROOF_EXPORT_BUCKET and SITE_SIGNING_KEY_PATH. For private deployments, installer patch adds proof-export hook but keep feature off by default. Monitor metric `proofs.signing.failures` and set paging threshold at 5/min.
validation_summary: Signed receipts validated against site public key during e2e run. Proof bundle schema v1 defined in docs. KMS adapters validate key metadata and will reject keys missing region or provider claims.
post_merge_tasks: 1) Run security rotation to create site signing key in HSM and provision path for bundler; 2) Add tenant-level entries to onboarding checklist; 3) Educate SRE on emergency disable env var; 4) Schedule audit with compliance team to sign off on proof schema.
special_considerations: Feature is intended for enterprise customers with strict audit needs. Keep export retention configurable to meet different jurisdictions. For high-volume tenants, bundle size and signing throughput may need autoscaling of the bundler service.
